analysis.title: US CPI: Easing but not pleasing
key_insights: October US CPI rose 0.4% mom against Bloomberg consensus of 0.3%, after a 0.6% mom rise in September. Berenberg says this is still well above the level at which the Fed is comfortable.
Berenberg says the October CPI was the last inflation data point before the Fed meeting on 9 December and gives the Fed no reason to relax. A stable labour market lets the Fed focus on inflation.

Markets price a 98% probability of a 25bp Fed hike to a 4.00%-4.25% target range on 9 December, and Berenberg agrees. The probability of a further hike in early 2027, above Berenberg's current forecast, has increased. The outcome depends on Middle East developments and energy prices.
Energy prices rose 0.7% mom in October after a 5.2% rise in September. Transportation services rose 0.8% mom, which Berenberg reads as high fuel costs being passed on to customers.

Services less energy services rose 0.3% mom and food rose 0.5% mom. Core CPI (ex food and energy) rose 0.3% mom, the same as September. Berenberg calls this a broader-based surge in inflation than the Fed would like.
No year-over-year CPI figure was published, because the October 2025 index was never produced during last year's government shutdown, so there is no comparable baseline.

Fed Governor Waller said in London that a December hike looks like a foregone conclusion and the open question is 25bp or 50bp. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has given no forward guidance, so investors are watching governors such as Waller.

Waller said he leans toward 25bp if October monthly inflation improves, but that a stronger move may be needed if core CPI stays around 0.3% or higher. Berenberg still considers a 50bp hike unlikely but sees Waller's comments as upside risk to its view of one more hike.

tension_points.bull_case: A 25bp hike is the base case. Waller leans toward 25bp if October monthly inflation improves, and markets price 98% for 25bp to 4.00%-4.25%.
tension_points.bear_case: A 50bp hike may be needed if core CPI stays around 0.3% or higher, per Waller. Berenberg sees this as upside risk to its one-more-hike view.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core CPI around 0.3% or higher, as in the past two monthly readings, would argue for a stronger policy move than 25bp.

theme_stances.key_argument: Inflation remains well above the Fed's comfort level and the labour market is stable, so the Fed can focus on tackling inflation.
